es: Presentar una minininvestigación: resultados con comparativos, un límite, respuesta a dudas y siguiente paso.

teaching.en: Today I will present the findings of our investigation.
teaching.es: Hoy presentaré los resultados de nuestra investigación.
teaching.explanationEs: Findings son los hallazgos. Se abre la presentación anunciando qué vas a mostrar.
teaching.audioText: Today I will present the findings of our investigation.

teaching.en: Our sample was small, so it may not be representative of all students.
teaching.es: Nuestra muestra era pequeña, así que puede no ser representativa de todos los alumnos.
teaching.explanationEs: Representative = que refleja a todo el grupo. May not be admite el límite sin exagerar.
segments: Our sample was small, so it may
not be representative of all students.
teaching.audioText: Our sample was small, so it may not be representative of all students.

teaching.en: Someone in the audience asked whether the results were reliable.
teaching.es: Alguien del público preguntó si los resultados eran fiables.
teaching.explanationEs: Whether introduce una pregunta indirecta («si»). Reliable = en lo que se puede confiar.
teaching.audioText: Someone in the audience asked whether the results were reliable.

teaching.en: That is a fair doubt, because all the respondents came from one school.
teaching.es: Es una duda justa, porque todos los encuestados venían de un colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: That is a fair doubt reconoce la objeción con respeto antes de explicarla.
segments: That is a fair doubt, because all
the respondents came from one school.
teaching.audioText: That is a fair doubt, because all the respondents came from one school.

teaching.en: Further research should include students from different schools.
teaching.es: Futuras investigaciones deberían incluir alumnos de diferentes colegios.
teaching.explanationEs: Further research propone el siguiente paso. Should da la recomendación con suavidad.
teaching.audioText: Further research should include students from different schools.

choices.text: All the students belong to one team.
The students do not exercise at all.

feedback.es: El orador dice que todos juegan en el mismo equipo: los participantes son muy parecidos y la muestra es limitada.

origin.audio: We asked forty students about sleep and exercise. The more they exercise, the better they sleep. However, all of them play in the same team.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuanto más duermen los alumnos, menos cansados se sienten.»

feedback.es: Cuanto más … menos … se dice the more …, the less ….

origin.text: The more students sleep, the ___ tired they feel.

prompt.es: Presenta tu investigación y contesta a la duda del público.

answer.text: Today I will present the findings of our investigation. We asked fifty students at our school whether they use their phones late and how many hours they sleep. Nearly half of the respondents, twenty-two students, sleep less than seven hours, and twice as many boys as girls use their phones for more than three hours. However, the main limitation is that we asked only one school. Someone in the audience asked whether the results prove that phones make students tired. That is a fair doubt, but the results only suggest a link, because our sample was small. Further research should include students from more schools.
accepted: Today I will present the findings of our investigation. We asked fifty students at our school whether they use their phones late and how many hours they sleep. Nearly half of the respondents, twenty-two students, sleep less than seven hours, and twice as many boys as girls use their phones for more than three hours. However, the main limitation is that we asked only one school. Someone in the audience asked whether the results prove that phones make students tired. That is a fair doubt, but the results only suggest a link, because our sample was small. Further research should include students from more schools.

Today I will present the findings of our investigation. We surveyed fifty students from our school about their phone use and their sleep. Almost half of the respondents, twenty-two students, sleep less than seven hours, and two times as many boys as girls use their phones for more than three hours. However, the main limitation is that we only asked one school. Someone asked whether the results prove that phones make students tired. That is a fair doubt, but the results suggest a link, not a cause, because the sample was small. More research should include students from other schools.

feedback.es: Una presentación completa abre, da resultados con comparativos, reconoce un límite, responde a la duda con prudencia y propone un paso.

origin.text: Presenta tu minininvestigación a la clase. Pregunta: ¿los alumnos que usan más el móvil duermen menos? Muestra: 50 alumnos de tu colegio. Resultados: 22 duermen menos de siete horas (casi la mitad); el doble de chicos que de chicas usa el móvil más de tres horas. Límite: solo un colegio. Duda del público: «¿Demuestra tu encuesta que el móvil cansa a los alumnos?». Respóndela con prudencia y propón un siguiente paso.

feedback.es: Ambas partes llevan the + comparativo: the more …, the better …; best sería un superlativo.
